6. Project Summary (Max 200 words):
The Urban Canopy Mapping Initiative aims to develop a validated methodology for mapping tree
canopy cover at sub-metre resolution across selected public housing estates in Singapore. Using
a combination of aerial LiDAR data (acquired via drone survey) and satellite multispectral
imagery, the project will produce a baseline canopy dataset that can inform urban heat island
mitigation and green space planning. The initiative will also pilot a citizen-science validation
protocol, engaging residents to ground-truth tree locations in two representative precincts
(Tampines and Jurong West). Outputs will include an open-access GIS layer, a technical
methodology report, and a policy brief for HDB and NParks. The project builds on preliminary
work by the PI on vegetation indices in tropical cities and responds directly to the National
Adaptation Framework’s call for enhanced urban greening data.

3. Co-Investigators (Co-I):

b) Ms. Nurul Huda, Research Associate, Centre for Remote Sensing (CRS)

4. Project Duration:
Proposed Start Date: 1 January 2021
Proposed End Date: 31 December 2022 (24 months)

5. Total Funding Requested:
SGD 55,000 (Revised from initial request of SGD 60,000 – see Section C, Note 1)

6. Project Summary (Max 200 words):
The Urban Canopy Mapping Initiative aims to develop a validated methodology for mapping tree
canopy cover at sub-metre resolution across selected public housing estates in Singapore. Using
a combination of aerial LiDAR data (acquired via drone survey) and satellite multispectral
imagery, the project will produce a baseline canopy dataset that can inform urban heat island
mitigation and green space planning. The initiative will also pilot a citizen-science validation
protocol, engaging residents to ground-truth tree locations in two representative precincts
(Tampines and Jurong West). Outputs will include an open-access GIS layer, a technical
methodology report, and a policy brief for HDB and NParks. The project builds on preliminary
work by the PI on vegetation indices in tropical cities and responds directly to the National
Adaptation Framework’s call for enhanced urban greening data.

The funding application shows Dr. Priya Raman funding_approval_amount of 50000 SGD. Record status: historical.
